deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is finding the critical (buckling) load P of a column of length a whose bending stiffness varies along its length. Earlier he treated a stiffness of Ekk(α+βx/a)^4. On this page he generalises to a power law of arbitrary exponent.

1. The equation. Put s = α + βx/a and n² = P a²/(β² Ekk), and let the stiffness at M be Ekk·s^{4λ}. The buckling equation, with derivatives taken in s, is s^{4λ} y'' + n² y = 0. Euler seeks values of λ for which this can be integrated in finite terms.

2. Removing the imaginaries for the moment. He writes n² = −m², giving s^{4λ}y'' = m²y. He then sets y = exp(φ)·z with φ = −m s^{1−2λ}/(2λ−1). Then φ' = m s^{−2λ} and φ'' = −2λ m s^{−2λ−1}. The term φ'² s^{4λ} = m² cancels exactly, which leaves z'' + 2m s^{−2λ} z' − 2λ m s^{−2λ−1} z = 0. This is the printed equation and it is correct.

3. The series. Try z = Σ a_k s^{μ_k} with μ_k = λ + k(2λ−1). Matching powers gives the recursion a_k = −μ_{k−1}(μ_{k−1}−1) a_{k−1} / (2mk(2λ−1)). This reproduces B, C and D exactly, and the leading exponent λ is forced.

4. When the series stops. It terminates exactly when μ_k(μ_k−1) = 0 for some k. That happens for λ = k/(2k+1) or λ = (k+1)/(2k+1), i.e. λ = 0, 1, 1/3, 2/3, 2/5, 3/5, ...
- In Riccati form this is the classical Bernoulli condition: the exponent −4λ must have the form −4k/(2k±1).
- In modern terms, y = √s·Z_ν(c s^{1−2λ}) with ν = 1/(2(2λ−1)), a Bessel function. The finite cases are the half-integer orders, i.e. the elementary-function cases.
- λ = 1 gives B = 0 and y = s e^{−m/s}, which is the previous page's case.
- Otherwise the series diverges, since the ratio of successive terms grows like k/m. It is then only an asymptotic series in 1/n.

5. Returning to real form (XXIV). With m = n√−1 and v = (2λ−1)s^{2λ−1}, the exponential becomes cos(n/v) − i sin(n/v). The next page combines this with the conjugate solution to get a real general integral.

6. Structure of the ansatz. The factor s^λ·exp(±i n/v) is exactly the Liouville–Green (WKB) form: amplitude Q^{−1/4} and phase ∫√Q, with Q = n² s^{−4λ}. The series in powers of 1/n is the full asymptotic expansion in the large parameter n.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page: the transformed equation and the coefficients B, C, D all check.
Euler does not flag that λ = 1/2 is excluded: there 2λ−1 = 0 and the substitution breaks down. That case is an Euler–Cauchy equation s²y''+n²y=0 with power or logarithmic solutions.
He does not state explicitly here that the series terminates only for λ = k/(2k+1) or (k+1)/(2k+1), nor that otherwise it diverges. It may be addressed on following pages.

ideas.what: Reducing a variable-stiffness buckling equation s^{4λ}y''+n²y=0 by an exponential factor exp(∫ m s^{-2λ}ds), followed by a descending power series
ideas.modern_name: Liouville–Green / WKB form with its asymptotic series; Bessel-type equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Liouville and Green (1837) for the LG approximation; Riccati equation work by D. Bernoulli and Euler (1720s–1730s)
ideas.where_published: Euler's Riccati papers (e.g. E31 and others) and Institutiones calculi integralis vol. II (E366); E238 itself is discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: Termination of the series giving elementary closed-form solutions for special λ
ideas.modern_name: Bernoulli integrability condition for the Riccati equation; half-integer-order Bessel functions
ideas.where_published: Euler's Riccati papers; Institutiones calculi integralis II

ideas.what: Combining conjugate complex solutions with conjugate constants to get a real general integral
ideas.modern_name: Real form of the complex general solution
ideas.where_published: E62 and related papers on linear ODEs

ideas.what: Buckling load of columns with power-law stiffness

missed.claim: Euler's ansatz, the amplitude s^λ times exp(±i n/v) times a series in 1/n, is exactly the Liouville–Green/WKB form with its full asymptotic expansion in the large parameter n. This appears about 80 years before Liouville and Green, and in a structural-stability context. Historians usually link E238 to Bessel functions; the WKB reading is less commonly emphasised (unsure whether Truesdell notes it).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Antedates the asymptotic-expansion viewpoint (high-load or slender limit) for variable-coefficient eigenvalue problems in buckling. This is a minor historical-priority note.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the known Riccati/Bessel machinery and E238 is well studied by Truesdell. The only mildly notable point is that the ansatz is precisely the full WKB/Liouville–Green expansion, which is probably under-remarked.
